title: Media playback automation not working
body:

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
I did some test using NodeRed and found there is a specific pattern:
1. When homepod is in 'Standby' status ,  you send a TTS, then you sure will get a timeout error.
2. Whenever homepod is not in 'Standy' , eg. 'Pause',  'Playing' status , there is no problem it will play the TTS quickly.
The problem here is : it's not clear when will the Homepod goes into 'Standby' status. It seems when a previous TTS message was successfully played, Homepod will turn into 'Standby'.  and if you send TTS again, it will fail for sure. but the next attempt will be successfully.
As  I'm only using homepod to play TTS notifications for now , so i did a workaround in NodeRed just to retry playing when it fails.....
Hope this problem can be fixed in the pyatv integration. Otherwise to be fixed by apple, as it could be a bug/or a behavior change in Homepod recent firmware updates.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Guys, I have found a workaround. Here's what I did,

1. Install this add-on via HACS https://github.com/amitfin/retry
2. Change your scripts/automations like this

For media files
```
alias: Play Some File
sequence:
  - service: media_player.volume_set
    data:
      volume_level: 0.8
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.homepod_1
  - service: retry.call
    data:
      service: media_player.play_media
      retries: 5
      media_content_id: media-source://media_source/local/some_file.mp3
      media_content_type: music
      announce: true
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.homepod_1
mode: single
icon: mdi:play
```

For TTS
```
alias: Play TTS
fields:
  message:
    name: Message
    description: The message to be played.
sequence:
  - service: media_player.volume_set
    data:
      volume_level: 0.8
    target:
      entity_id: media_player.homepod_1
  - service: retry.call
    data:
      service: tts.amazon_polly_say
      retries: 5
      cache: true
      entity_id: media_player.homepod_1
      message: "{{ message }}"
mode: single
icon: mdi:microphone-message
```

I'm using scripts and calling them from automations. This same concept should work even without scripts.

Hehe, I didn't want to mess up with libraries.. this was just a quick test changing the timeout manually, since this was just a single line of code I took this route.

open ha cli
then type `login`
it should give you a prompt `#`
type: `docker exec -it $(docker ps -f name=homeassistant -q) bash`
now you should be inside the homeassistant container
open the pyatv file: `vi /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pyatv/support/http.py`
change the timeout from 4 to 10
before: `async with async_timeout.timeout(4):`
after: `async with async_timeout.timeout(10):`
restart your homeassistant and you should be good to go!

No, you are not! Sorry for my lack of "clear" instructions! but, there are 2 ways to gain access:

1 - it seems like the login command only works via console (local) and not via the "default" SSH addon -> https://community.home-assistant.io/t/how-to-get-access-at-damn-host-system/96549/85 . So, you must use your VM console, KVM or plug a keyboard and monitor to your box and run the commands from there.

2 - Install the SSH addon that allows you to disable "Protection Mode" - https://github.com/hassio-addons/addon-ssh - Once you login via SSH (with protection mode disabled), you just need to run the docker command to access the homeassistant container, and change timeout value as mentioned before.

![ssh-addon](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3930500/229360616-7c5daaef-99f5-4244-93c4-335ab67f93f0.png)


```
➜  ~ docker exec -it homeassistant bash
bash-5.1# 
```

I hope this helps! 

---
quick update: I've been using this "workaround/fix" for a day, and so far, no timeouts!  but still... a big delay was introduced - not the end of the world, but if we could reduce this to < 4s as before it would be great!
